response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile full-stack engineer with 15+ years of delivery experience, strong testing/craftsmanship culture, and high-performance distributed systems exposure (low-latency microservices at Sociomantic). However, the role centers on C++/STL development for industrial automation platforms, and the resume shows only ~6 months of professional C++ work (National Instruments, 2014-2015) plus an academic project — over a decade ago. There is no evidence of IEC 62443 / Secure Development Lifecycle practice, MQTT or industrial protocols (Modbus, OPC UA, IEC 61850), message-broker architectures, or Azure. The core technical requirement is essentially unmet, so despite strong general engineering ability this is a poor match for a mid-senior C++ position.
strengths: 15+ years of broad engineering experience with strong software craftsmanship (TDD, CI/CD, pairing)
Proven high-performance, low-latency distributed systems work (async I/O, fibers, caching, microservices at scale)
Demonstrated ownership, mentoring and communication via workshops, talks, open-source projects and founding GISCollective
concerns: Minimal and dated C++/STL experience (~6 months in 2014-2015); primary stack is TypeScript/Node.js
No industrial automation, IoT protocol (MQTT, Modbus, OPC UA) or message-broker architecture experience shown
No evidence of secure development lifecycle or IEC 62443 industrial cybersecurity expertise

key_factors.factor: Industrial automation, IoT and security standards (IEC 62443) gap
